questions.prompt: What does sales intelligence primarily turn into better decisions?
questions.explanation: Sales intelligence is the practice of turning reliable CRM and activity data into decisions that help sales teams prioritise action.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of an intent signal on a lead?
questions.explanation: Engagement such as attending a webinar signals buying intent, while firmographic details like employee count are company fit signals.

questions.prompt: In the NexaFlow lifecycle, which stage normally comes right after MQL?
questions.explanation: A marketing-qualified lead (MQL) becomes a sales-qualified lead (SQL) once sales confirms fit and intent.

questions.prompt: Why is cleaning data before analysis important?
options: It replaces the need for a CRM
questions.explanation: Clean data is a prerequisite for trustworthy KPIs, funnel reporting and CRM governance.

questions.prompt: Which action best addresses duplicate lead records?
options: Merge or de-duplicate on a unique identifier
Delete every row with similar names
questions.explanation: Duplicates are resolved by matching unique identifiers or business keys, not by guessing from similar names.

questions.prompt: A standardised value list for the Source field would use…
options: A fixed set such as Webinar, Inbound, Referral
Free text typed differently each time
questions.explanation: Standardising fields to a fixed value list keeps analytics grouping consistent.

questions.prompt: What should come first when building a sales dashboard?
questions.explanation: A good dashboard starts with clear, consistent KPI definitions so every viewer reads the same numbers.

questions.prompt: A lead funnel visualises…
questions.explanation: A funnel shows how many leads sit at each lifecycle stage and where conversion drops off.

questions.prompt: Which is a measure rather than a dimension?
questions.explanation: Pipeline value is a numeric measure; industry, source and region are dimensions used to slice it.

questions.prompt: CRM field governance defines…
options: Which data is required and who keeps it trustworthy
The colour of the CRM interface
How many users can log in
questions.explanation: Governance sets required fields, owners and standards so CRM records stay reliable.

questions.prompt: Why does every lead need a clear owner?
questions.explanation: An owner is accountable for acting on the lead, which prevents records from being lost.

questions.prompt: Stage history matters because it…
questions.explanation: Stage history creates an auditable record of how and when a lead progressed through the lifecycle.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between an MQL and an SQL?
options: MQL fits marketing criteria; SQL is qualified by sales
questions.explanation: An MQL meets marketing-fit criteria; sales confirms fit and intent to turn it into an SQL.

questions.prompt: A lead is considered stale when…
options: It has had no activity for several days
It belongs to a large company
questions.explanation: Staleness is measured by days without activity, which is why next actions and activity logging matter.

questions.prompt: Setting a next action date on every lead helps…
options: Ensure no lead slips through the cracks
questions.explanation: A next action date creates a commitment that keeps follow-up cadence visible and measurable.

quizzes.title: Generative AI for sales intelligence check

questions.prompt: Before acting on an AI research output, you should…
options: Verify the claims against reliable sources
Send it immediately to the prospect
questions.explanation: AI can accelerate first drafts, but people must verify conclusions before taking action.

questions.prompt: A well-written prompt for lead research includes…
options: Context about the company and the goal
questions.explanation: Contextual prompts with a clear goal produce more useful simulated outputs.

questions.prompt: Why keep human judgement at the centre of AI-assisted sales work?
options: AI can hallucinate facts and miss context
AI always needs an API key
Humans are slower but less accurate
It is a legal requirement everywhere
questions.explanation: AI outputs are simulated or probabilistic, so human review protects accuracy and relationships.

questions.prompt: In a workflow, a trigger is…
options: The event that starts the process
questions.explanation: Workflows make repeatable work visible by starting from a defined trigger event.

questions.prompt: Why include a human approval step in an AI follow-up workflow?
options: No message should be sent without human review
questions.explanation: Human approval keeps AI-suggested messages accurate, appropriate and safe to send.

questions.prompt: A no-code automation tool is best used for…
options: Repeatable rules-based steps like lead routing
questions.explanation: No-code tools automate predictable, rule-based operations such as scoring, routing and alerts.

questions.prompt: Competitive intelligence should be based on…
questions.explanation: Evidence-based, verifiable comparisons keep competitive intelligence relevant and credible.

questions.prompt: When comparing competitors, you should…
options: Use the same criteria for every competitor
Change criteria to favour one vendor
questions.explanation: A fair comparison applies consistent criteria across all competitors.

questions.prompt: A competitor brief is most useful when it is…
options: Relevant to a specific sales context
questions.explanation: Intelligence only helps when it is relevant, verifiable and actionable for the situation at hand.

questions.prompt: A useful SOP explains…
options: Purpose, inputs, steps, owner and exception path
questions.explanation: A useful SOP covers why the process exists, what it needs, the steps, the owner and how exceptions are handled.

questions.prompt: Why does every SOP need a named process owner?
options: Someone is accountable for keeping it current
questions.explanation: A process owner keeps the SOP accurate, current and followed.

questions.prompt: The exception path in an SOP handles…
options: Cases that do not fit the standard steps
questions.explanation: An exception path defines what happens when the standard flow does not apply.

questions.prompt: Which is one of the ten capstone deliverables?
questions.explanation: The capstone has ten deliverables including data cleaning, lead scoring, assignment rules, dashboards and an SOP library.

questions.prompt: A portfolio-ready capstone shows…
options: A complete system, not just notes
questions.explanation: Employers want evidence of a complete, working sales intelligence system built end to end.

questions.prompt: The final capstone deliverable is…
questions.explanation: The capstone ends with a management report or presentation that communicates the built system.

assignments.title: Map your sales funnel
assignments.instructions: Draw the NexaFlow lead lifecycle from NEW to CLOSED_WON / CLOSED_LOST. For each stage, write one sentence explaining what must happen for a lead to move forward and who is responsible. Submit as text or a link to your diagram.
assignments.rubric: Completeness of stages (40%) · clarity of the movement criteria (40%) · ownership assigned (20%)

assignments.title: Clean a demo dataset
assignments.instructions: Using the fictional lead data in the CRM Lab, list three data-quality issues you can find (for example missing owners or inconsistent sources) and describe how you would clean each one in a spreadsheet. Submit your findings and your proposed cleaning steps.
assignments.rubric: Real issues identified (40%) · practical cleaning steps (40%) · clear write-up (20%)

assignments.title: Define five sales KPIs
assignments.instructions: Define five KPIs a sales operations manager should track, using the Analytics page as inspiration. For each KPI give: name, definition, formula or calculation, and why it matters.
assignments.rubric: Five KPIs defined (30%) · formulas correct (40%) · business rationale (30%)

assignments.title: CRM field standards
assignments.instructions: Write a one-page CRM field governance standard for NexaFlow: which lead fields are required, which use a fixed value list, who owns data quality, and how duplicates are handled.
assignments.rubric: Required fields defined (35%) · value lists (30%) · ownership and dedupe rules (35%)

assignments.title: Lead routing plan
assignments.instructions: Design a lead scoring and routing plan for a fictional B2B SaaS company. Define 3–5 scoring factors with points, 3–4 assignment rules in priority order, and explain how workload is considered.
assignments.rubric: Scoring factors defined (35%) · assignment rules in priority order (35%) · workload handling (30%)

assignments.title: AI research prompt set
assignments.instructions: Write three prompts a sales rep could use for lead research: one for company research, one for lead qualification and one for a follow-up draft. Test each in the AI Practice Lab and paste the simulated outputs with your verification notes.
assignments.rubric: Three prompts written (30%) · used in the AI lab (30%) · verification notes show human review (40%)

assignments.title: Automation workflow map
assignments.instructions: Map one automation workflow for NexaFlow (for example stale-lead escalation). Show the trigger, each step, the decision points, the human approval steps and the final action.
assignments.rubric: Trigger and steps clear (40%) · decision and approval points (40%) · final action defined (20%)

assignments.title: Competitor brief
assignments.instructions: Create a one-page competitive intelligence brief for a fictional workflow-automation company: three competitors, a consistent comparison criteria table, and three actionable takeaways for sales.
assignments.rubric: Three competitors compared (40%) · consistent criteria (30%) · actionable takeaways (30%)

assignments.title: Write a usable SOP
assignments.instructions: Write a complete SOP for one sales operations process (for example: handling a new inbound lead). Include purpose, inputs, numbered steps, process owner and an exception path.
assignments.rubric: All SOP sections present (50%) · steps actionable (30%) · owner and exceptions defined (20%)

assignments.title: Capstone delivery plan
assignments.instructions: List all ten capstone deliverables, mark which ones you have already practised in this platform, and write a two-week plan with a deadline for each remaining deliverable.
assignments.rubric: All ten deliverables listed (40%) · progress marked honestly (30%) · realistic plan (30%)
